mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains > 5.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations, which compresses the real return on equities and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day and 60-day forward returns are both positive and statistically significantly greater than the 30-day rolling mean during the inflation spike (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly HOUST (household utilization rate) above 12% for two consecutive months signals tight credit conditions and impending demand collapse, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive and statistically higher than the 5-day baseline during the trigger (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 10,000 for three consecutive months indicates labor market strengthening, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 10,000 each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant versus the 60-day rolling mean during the labor expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% for two consecutive months reflects supply-side contraction, lowering growth expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significantly higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the contraction (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales activity) exceeds 710,000 for three consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant versus the 60-day rolling mean during the demand surge (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual decline in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment rate) for two consecutive months creates a 'soft landing' expectation, lowering real rate pressure and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls for two consecutive months AND UNRATE falls for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual softening in monetary policy and labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive versus the 30-day rolling mean during the dual softening (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, the labor market becomes more accommodative, raising optimism about growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant versus the 20-day rolling mean during the easing (t-test p > 0.05).
